This perspective reframes the local LLM value proposition from purely economic (cheaper than subscriptions) to organizational and philosophical (data sovereignty and privacy). The insight that local LLMs replaced not cloud APIs but rather all the data practitioners were "never comfortable sending to the cloud" highlights a critical use case often overlooked in cost-benefit analyses.

For enterprises, governments, and individuals handling sensitive information—medical records, financial data, proprietary research, personal communications—local inference isn't just a cost optimization, it's a compliance and risk management requirement. This category of users will adopt local LLMs regardless of whether they're cheaper, because closed-source cloud APIs are simply not an option for their use cases.

This framing matters for practitioners deciding between local and cloud deployment: the decision isn't always about tokens-per-dollar, but about what data can legally and ethically be sent outside organizational boundaries.
